newsitem.title: INDIA: Profit-taking erases gains on Delhi bourse.
newsitem.headline: Profit-taking erases gains on Delhi bourse.

text.p: Share prices ended lower in mixed trade on the Delhi Stock Exchange on Monday as profit-taking wiped out early gains, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 1.13 points lower at 909.33 points.
The index had leapt to 920.90 at 12.45 p.m. (0715 GMT).
Traders said speculators pocketed profits after prices soared in early trade on purchases by foreign and domestic financial institutions at the start of the new settlement period.
"Profit-taking by speculators has brought down the prices," said one broker.
Vijay Aggarwal of brokers Mass Financial Services said: "The market has turned highly bullish and the share prices are expected to rise in the near future."
State Bank of India ended 3.20 rupees higher at 354.40 on foreign buying, brokers said.
